papers.title: Boatbuilder's note
lines: Hooker, thirty-two foot, black hull, brown sails. Sound as a bell and twice as loud when she goes about.
The first mate has been drinking since Thursday. The second mate is the dog.

papers.title: Poetry-lover's postcard
lines: I stood on the shore where the poet stood, and I thought a great thought, and it blew away.
A man with a flask told me this is the usual result. He gave me tea and a second chance.

papers.title: Limerick on a beermat
lines: There once was a poet from Limerick, / who wrote verses that went on for ... a while.
(The rest is on the other beermat. We lost it. It was better.)

papers.title: Knitter's pattern
lines: Every family has its own stitch, they say, so a drowned man can be named by his sleeve.
I do not believe it, but I knit my brother's with a very clear pattern, just in case.

trail.clue: A knitter's tin of coins lies under a flat stone near the hedge.

papers.title: Ceili band booking
lines: Seven musicians, a bodhrán and an accordion with a grudge. Fee: three pounds, a ham sandwich and a lift home.
Please do not ask for 'Whiskey in the Jar'. Please do not ask twice.

papers.title: Boatman's tally
lines: Funghi the dolphin came by twice. Both times the tourists cheered and then asked if he was real.
I told them he was. He bowed. Everyone clapped, including the gulls.

trail.clue: A boat tour left behind a small treasure near the big rock, 'for whoever is looking'.

papers.title: Irish lesson note
lines: Dia duit: God to you. Dia is Muire duit: God and Mary to you. A greeting that answers itself.
Slán abhaile: safe home. We say it to everyone, even the man who stole the milk bottles.
